short_title: Economic value lost with the seagrass (2023)
title: Economic losses related to the reduction of Posidonia ecosystem services in the Gulf of Gabes (Southern Mediterranean Sea)
summary: Reports that about 90% of the original seagrass area has been lost since the 1970s. Estimates the value lost in 2014 at 105 million euros (fishing and carbon storage), about 115% of the added value of the fertiliser factories that year.

findings.headline: About 90% of the original seagrass has been lost
findings.summary: More than 500 million tonnes of wet phosphogypsum have been discharged since the 1970s. The authors link this to the loss of about 90% of the original seagrass area.
findings.headline_original: About 90% of the original seagrass area is gone
findings.summary_original: More than 500 million tonnes of wet phosphogypsum discharged since the 1970s are linked to the loss of about 90% of the initial seagrass surface.

findings.headline: The 2014 losses equal about 115% of what the factories added in value
findings.summary: The authors estimate the economic loss in 2014 at 105 million euros. That is about 115% of the added value of the Gabès fertiliser factories that year.
findings.headline_original: Value lost in 2014 equals about 115% of the factories' added value
findings.summary_original: Economic losses estimated at 105 million euros in 2014, around 115% of the added value of the Gabès fertilizer factories for the same year.
